title: torus
body:
## torus

Creates a closed ring (torus) of quads lying in the local XY plane around the local Z axis: majorRadius is the distance from centre to the middle of the tube and minorRadius is the tube radius. majorSegments divides the ring and minorSegments divides the tube cross-section. Use it for O-rings, seals and annular markers.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Keep minorRadius below majorRadius; otherwise the tube passes through the axis and the surface self-intersects.
- The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

Native binding: `torus`. Output kind: `["data"]`.

| Input port | Multiplicity | Required | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `material` | one node | yes | `material` |

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `majorRadius` | Distance from the torus centre to the centre line of its tube, in the local XY plane; the overall outer radius is majorRadius + minorRadius. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"exclusiveMinimum":true}` | `1` |
| `minorRadius` | Radius of the tube cross-section. It should stay below majorRadius so the hole remains open. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"exclusiveMinimum":true}` | `0.25` |
| `majorSegments` | Number of divisions around the ring (about local Z). Increase it for large rings seen close up. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":3,"maximum":256}` | `32` |
| `minorSegments` | Number of divisions around the tube cross-section. The face count is majorSegments times minorSegments. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":3,"maximum":256}` | `16` |
| `centre` | World position [x, y, z] of the centre of the ring. Schemaxis assigns it as the object's location, so the mesh itself stays about the local origin and later modifiers that work about that origin (mirror, bend, twist) use this point. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `smoothShading` | When true, every face of the generated torus is marked smooth so Blender interpolates normals and the tessellated surface renders without visible facets; when false the faces render flat. Geometry and vertex positions are identical either way. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `false` |
